headline: Fresh records meet rising unease over AI-spending excess
body: Wall Street enters the week carrying real momentum but a noticeably shakier mood. Friday's tech-led rally pushed the Nasdaq 100 to a fresh record close, and the S&P 500 and Dow notched gains to start October (S&P 500 up roughly a quarter percent to 7,670 on Thursday), with softer recent jobs data easing worries that the Fed needs to stay restrictive. But Monday has given some of that back, with the S&P 500 slipping modestly from Friday's highs. The pattern looks less like a market rolling over than one that sprinted into records and is now catching its breath, pricing in rate-cut relief without fully shaking off the choppiness that higher long-term yields caused earlier in the quarter.

The more telling tension is around AI spending itself. Nvidia actually fell Friday even as OpenAI's reported $500 billion compute commitment briefly lifted AI-adjacent names, a sign investors are growing more selective about which capex announcements they'll reward. Hyperscalers keep raising their AI budgets, yet prominent voices (Ray Dalio drawing 1929/dot-com comparisons, Jamie Dimon flagging correction odds well above what's priced in) are feeding a live bubble debate. Retail chatter reinforces the uneasy tone: WallStreetBets sentiment swung sharply negative overnight, driven less by any single stock story than a viral large-margin-call thread — more a read on frayed nerves and loss-aversion than organized bearish positioning.
